summary: Correct, minimal, and well-scoped implementation that makes the train/val overfit gap observable in Phase 2 evolution logs. Three production files touched (config.py, log_progress.py, evox_runner.py) for a total of +38/-0 LOC. Division-by-zero is guarded; None values are guarded; threshold is config-driven; warning message is clear and actionable. Critical bonus: the evox_runner.py change wires robust_stats into the NSGA-II fallback's maybe_log_generation call, fixing a real wiring gap that would otherwise have prevented the warning from ever firing in the NSGA-II path (the NSGA-III path already had the wiring). The two pre-existing config constants bundled in this PR (MAX_TIME_EXIT_RETURN_PCT, TRADE_SUPPORT_PENALTY_EXPONENT) are noted by the spec reviewer and are low-severity. All 49 relevant tests pass; the 3 failures in test_crash_fix_and_run_logging.py are pre-existing on main and unrelated to this change.

correctness.ratio_calculation: VERIFIED. ratio = max_return_pct / max_robust_return_pct. Tested by hand with five scenarios: above threshold (7.5x → warning fires), below threshold (2.0x → no warning), exactly at threshold (3.0x → no warning, strict >), division by zero (denominator=0 → no warning), None numerator (max_return_pct=None → no warning). All five behave as expected.
correctness.division_by_zero_guard: PRESENT and CORRECT. The check `max_robust_return_pct > 0` is evaluated before the division. When max_robust_return_pct is 0 (or negative, though that's impossible by construction) the warning is silently suppressed rather than raising. The corresponding existing numeric path emits 'max_robust_return=0.00%%' in the INFO line, so the user still sees the raw value and understands the gap.
correctness.none_safety: VERIFIED. Both `max_return_pct is not None` and `max_robust_return_pct is not None` are checked. log_generation() remains safe to call without any of the new kwargs (preserving the existing call-site contract used by phase 3 and other callers).
correctness.threshold_semantics: GOOD. Strict `>` comparison means a ratio of exactly 3.0x does not warn. This is the conventional behavior and avoids false positives right at the threshold. The threshold default of 3.0 is a reasonable starting point for the train/val gap.
correctness.nsga2_wiring_fix: BONUS FIX. The evox_runner.py change adds three new kwargs (mean_robust_return_pct, max_robust_return_pct, max_robust_sortino) to the maybe_log_generation call in _run_nsga2_fallback. Confirmed against main: this call site previously did NOT pass max_robust_return_pct, which would have caused the new overfit warning to never fire in the NSGA-II fallback path. The NSGA-III path (line 2563 in evox_runner.py) was already wired correctly. Without this change, only NSGA-III would have produced the warning — a real integration bug, fixed.
correctness.evox_runner_diff_line: robust_stats was already computed at line 1850 in the NSGA-II path (within the loop body) but was unused until this PR. The PR reuses it for the new logging. No new computation, no new dependencies.

security.concerns: None. Pure logging change. No I/O, no user input, no external calls, no eval/exec, no path traversal. The warning string is built with %-formatting from numeric values, so no format-string injection risk.

maintainability.config_driven_threshold: GOOD. PHASE2_OVERFIT_WARNING_RATIO lives in config.py with a clear three-line comment block describing the higher/lower tradeoff and the train-overfit-robust semantic. Users can tune sensitivity without touching code.
maintainability.warning_message_clarity: GOOD. Message includes raw values AND the ratio: 'max_return=15.00%% vs max_robust_return=2.00%% (7.5x overfit to train window!)'. Operator can immediately see both the absolute and relative gap. The 'overfit to train window!' suffix is mildly editorial but useful for non-expert operators.
maintainability.code_locality: GOOD. The warning block lives at the end of log_generation(), right after the INFO line, so anyone reading the function sees the entire generation-logging logic in one place. Threshold constant is imported via _cfg.
maintainability.backward_compatibility: VERIFIED. log_generation() and maybe_log_generation() keep the existing kwarg signatures; the new check is gated entirely on kwargs being provided. Pre-existing callers (Phase 3, etc.) that don't pass max_return_pct and max_robust_return_pct are unaffected.
maintainability.evox_runner_change_minimal: GOOD. Three kwargs added, no new variable, no restructured logic. Diff is +4 lines.
maintainability.docstring_update: MINOR. The config comment for PHASE2_OVERFIT_WARNING_RATIO is clear but does not mention the related PHASE2_MAX_TRAIN_VAL_GAP_PCT gate (16.0) that already exists upstream. A user tuning the warning threshold may also want to know the pool-admission gate exists. Optional cross-reference, non-blocking.

test_adequacy.pre_existing_failures: 3 tests in tests/unit/test_crash_fix_and_run_logging.py (test_run_log_file_created_and_contains_start_end, test_handler_detached_after_run, test_run_log_append_mode_across_two_runs) fail on BOTH main and fix/overfit-gap-logging. Verified by running the file on main: same 3 failures. These are unrelated to this PR.
test_adequacy.new_test_coverage: GAP. The PR adds no new tests. The existing test_log_progress.py tests cover the standard INFO-line emission but do not exercise the new overfit warning path. Recommended addition (not blocking): a TestOverfitWarning class with 4 cases — (1) ratio above threshold → warning fires, (2) ratio below threshold → no warning, (3) max_robust_return_pct=0 → no warning (div-by-zero guard), (4) max_return_pct=None → no warning (None guard). I manually verified all four scenarios in a sandbox and they behave correctly; encoding them as unit tests would prevent regression and document the contract.
test_adequacy.evox_runner_wiring_untested: GAP. The evox_runner.py change wires robust_stats into maybe_log_generation, but no test asserts that _run_nsga2_fallback's call includes max_robust_return_pct. A focused test that mocks maybe_log_generation and verifies the kwarg is passed would be valuable but is not strictly required.
test_adequacy.test_adequacy_summary: The 49 tests that pass are pre-existing tests of adjacent functionality; the new behavior is uncovered. Given the simplicity of the change (3 conditions in a single function) and the manual verification I performed, this is a low-severity gap. Recommend adding tests in a follow-up.

The behavior is simple and correct but currently uncovered.
Add a row for PHASE2_OVERFIT_WARNING_RATIO in the README config table near line 348 (next to PHASE2_MAX_TRAIN_VAL_GAP_PCT, which is the closest semantic neighbor).

Consider parameterizing the test_evox_runner.py test (or adding a new one) to assert that _run_nsga2_fallback passes max_robust_return_pct=... to maybe_log_generation. This regression-guard the wiring fix.

verdict_rationale: The core change is correct, secure, and minimal. The division-by-zero and None guards are present and verified. The threshold is config-driven, the warning message is clear and includes both raw values and the ratio, and the evox_runner.py change fixes a real wiring gap in the NSGA-II path. The bundled out-of-scope config constants are a non-issue (already on main). The only real concerns are (a) lack of unit tests for the new behavior and (b) missing README entry — both nits, neither blocking. The change is approved for merge.
